q: Multihost with the states DB in Redis on the master: the slave gets `connect ECONNREFUSED 192.168.1.10:6379` for the states DB while objects work. Redis on the master is version 7. What has to be changed?
facts: In /etc/redis/redis.conf on the master, extend `bind 127.0.0.1` with the master's LAN IP (e.g. `bind 127.0.0.1 192.168.1.10`) or use `bind 0.0.0.0` – only needed on the master
From Redis 7 on, protected mode must also be disabled: `protected-mode no`
Restart the Redis server afterwards (e.g. `sudo service redis-server restart`); the master's `iobroker setup custom` must use 0.0.0.0 as states DB host
evidence: ioBroker.docs/docs/en/config/multihost.md :: The line `bind 127.0.0.1` contained therein must be supplemented with the IP address of the network adapter so that the Redis server allows connections from outside.

q: I keep getting a js-controller notification in the "diskSpaceIssues" category although there are still ~10 GB free on my 256 GB SSD. When is this raised and how can I change the threshold?
facts: js-controller raises a warning-level notification (scope system, category diskSpaceIssues) when free disk space falls below a threshold
Default threshold is 5 % of the disk space
Override via the state system.host.<hostname>.diskWarning (value between 0 and 100)

q: Since moving states (and objects) to Redis my ioBroker is extremely slow and the admin takes minutes to load. `redis-cli DBSIZE` shows several hundred thousand keys. Someone suggested `redis-cli FLUSHALL`. Is that safe, and what are the alternatives?
facts: Identify the adapter creating huge numbers of datapoints and remove it (e.g. `iob stop <adapter>` / `iob del <adapter>`)
`redis-cli FLUSHALL` wipes the whole Redis DB – fine if only states are in Redis, but if objects are in Redis too all data is gone; afterwards `iob setup first` is required
Switching back to file-based DBs via `iob stop` + `iobroker setup custom` is recommended for fewer than 50,000 objects
